mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which positively impacts the S&P 500, leading to higher forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns despite a UNRATE decrease, or if Rank IC remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) above a 5% monthly growth signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur despite the housing starts growth, or Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS are low and UNRATE is high, it indicates economic stress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur despite low FEDFUNDS and high UNRATE, or Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP (GDPC1) reflects strong economic activity, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur despite GDP growth, or Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below a 2% monthly growth signals a slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur despite INDPRO decline, or Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising CPIAUCSL with increasing FEDFUNDS indicates tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur despite the conditions, or Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur despite RSAFS growth, or Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Growing payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur despite employment growth, or Rank IC is below 0.03.
